EDING.label: -ed / -ing 감정 형용사
EDING.tip: 내가 느끼면 -ed (I felt bored / I was inspired), 사물·상황이 느끼게 하면 -ing (It was boring / inspiring / challenging).

COMP.label: 비교급
COMP.tip: 긴 형용사는 more ~ than, 짧은 형용사는 -er (simpler, easier). '아주 더'는 very가 아니라 much more.

TENSE.label: 과거 이야기 시제
TENSE.tip: 경험(STAR) 답변은 처음부터 끝까지 과거형: felt, didn't need, was.

POS.label: 품사
POS.tip: 동사를 꾸미면 부사(quickly, flexibly), be·feel 뒤는 형용사(anxious, advantageous), 명사 앞엔 관사(an advantage).

PREP.label: 전치사
PREP.tip: 동사·형용사와 짝인 전치사를 통째로 외운다: sign up for, related to, helpful for, at a university, at night, downtown(전치사 없음).

ART.label: 관사·복수
ART.tip: 셀 수 있는 단수 명사엔 a/the, 일반적인 것은 복수: at a cafe, a kindergarten, all universities.

OBJ.label: 목적어 빠짐
OBJ.tip: inform / ask / remind 뒤엔 사람: inform you about, ask you to, remind me to.

SVA.label: 주어-동사 수일치
SVA.tip: every·each + 단수 동사 (every student has), 복수 주어 + 복수 동사 (online classes are).

KOR.label: 한국어식 표현
KOR.tip: '~해야 했다'는 had to, '보통 ~한다'는 typically. should는 조언·의무에만.

LINK.label: 연결어
LINK.tip: Although/While 문장엔 but을 같이 쓰지 않는다. Therefore는 진짜 결과일 때만, Nevertheless는 대조일 때만.

COLL.label: 단어 조합
COLL.tip: 자연스러운 짝으로: improve the quality of our lives, lead to + 명사/-ing, affect people(전치사 없음).

SPELL.label: 철자
SPELL.tip: 시험엔 맞춤법 검사가 없다. 마지막 1분은 철자만 본다.

prof.name: Dr. Alvarez
prof.text: This week, we are evaluating school calendar designs. Many educational systems follow a traditional calendar featuring a long summer vacation of two or three months. However, some districts have shifted to a year-round calendar. In a year-round system, students attend school for the same total number of days, but their time off is distributed into multiple shorter breaks throughout the year—such as a three-week break every season. I would like you to discuss which approach you think is better for students. Does the traditional long summer break provide essential benefits, or is a year-round schedule with frequent, shorter breaks more advantageous?

students.name: Liam
students.text: I strongly prefer the traditional calendar with a long summer break. Students undergo a tremendous amount of stress during the academic year, and they need a significant, uninterrupted block of time to truly decompress. Furthermore, a long summer allows teenagers to get part-time jobs, attend specialized summer camps, or travel extensively with their families. These real-world experiences are just as important for a student's overall development as classroom learning.

students.name: Maya
students.text: I have to disagree with Liam. The biggest issue with a long summer break is what educators call the 'summer slide.' Students often forget a large portion of the material they learned the previous year, forcing teachers to spend the first month of the new term reviewing old topics. A year-round schedule prevents this knowledge loss. Plus, having frequent, shorter breaks throughout the year prevents burnout much more effectively than waiting nine exhausting months for a vacation.

prof.name: Professor Thorne
prof.text: Welcome to our Business Management seminar. Today, we are discussing emerging trends in corporate structuring. Recently, several high-profile companies have tested a four-day workweek. In this model, employees work thirty-two hours over four days but receive the same compensation as a traditional forty-hour, five-day week. Proponents argue this arrangement improves work-life balance, while critics worry about a drop in overall productivity and operational coverage. Do you think adopting a four-day workweek is a smart long-term strategy for businesses? Why or why not?

students.name: Elena
students.text: I strongly believe that a four-day workweek is a great strategy. Employee burnout is a massive problem right now, leading to frequent mistakes and low morale. If people have a three-day weekend to truly disconnect and spend time with their families, they will return to work highly motivated. Because they are well-rested and energized, they can actually complete the same amount of work in four days as they previously did in five.

students.name: David
students.text: I disagree. While a four-day workweek sounds nice in theory, it just isn't practical for most businesses. Think about logistics companies, customer support centers, or retail stores—they need to be available to clients every single day. If a company reduces everyone's hours, management will be forced to hire additional staff just to cover the missing shifts. This would significantly increase payroll costs and ultimately make the business less competitive.

prof.text: Welcome, everyone. This week, we are looking at pricing strategies, specifically the widespread shift toward subscription-based models. In the past, consumers usually paid a one-time fee to own a product outright, such as a software program, a video game, or an album. Today, many companies instead charge a recurring monthly or annual fee for ongoing access to their products or services. I'd like to hear your thoughts on this trend. Do you think the shift toward subscription models is ultimately beneficial for consumers, or does it do more harm than good?

students.name: Alex
students.text: I believe subscription models are great for consumers because they significantly lower the initial cost of access. Instead of paying hundreds of dollars upfront for professional software or a massive media library, anyone can afford a small monthly fee. Plus, companies are incentivized to constantly improve their services and provide regular updates to keep their subscribers happy, so we always get the most updated version of the product.

students.name: Maria
students.text: I have to disagree. I think the subscription model is harmful because it usually costs consumers much more in the long run. There is also the issue of ownership; you never actually own the product. If you face financial trouble and have to cancel your subscription, you lose access to everything immediately. A one-time purchase gives consumers permanent ownership and much more control over their personal budgets.

Furthermore, these characteristics of the characters can help readers understand the author's messages more easily. For these reasons, I believe character development is the most important factor in storytelling.

discussion.note: 튜터가 '그래서 어떻게 되는가' 문장과 질문형 문장(where will the company's future leaders come from?)을 추가했다.

prof.name: Dr. Morgan
prof.text: In management, leaders use very different styles. Democratic leaders involve employees in decisions, while authoritarian leaders make decisions on their own and expect employees to follow them. Which leadership style do you think is more effective in the workplace? Why?

students.name: Andrew
students.text: Authoritarian leadership is more effective, especially in a crisis. Decisions are made quickly, and everyone knows exactly what to do.

students.name: Claire
students.text: Democratic leadership works better in the long run. When employees take part in decisions, they feel responsible for the results and work harder.

discussion.mine: Both Andrew and Claire made valid points, but I lean toward Claire's view. I strongly agree with the notion that democratic leadership is more effective than authoritarian leadership. This is because democratic leadership can give opportunities to develop themselves. For example, if many employees can participate in their work-decisions more directly, it can become helpful experiences to improve their results. According to recent research, many junior employees do not have enough opportunities to develop their skills since many bosses require to follow only their rules. Therefore, if companies implement the democratic leadership, I believe it will be a fascinating chance to develop employees' abilities.
discussion.tutor: Both Andrew and Claire made valid points, but I lean toward Claire's view. I strongly agree with the notion that democratic leadership is more effective than authoritarian leadership. This is because democratic leadership can give opportunities for employees to develop themselves. For example, if many employees can participate in their work-decisions more directly, it can improve their results in the workplace. When employees feel free to speak their opinions and work as a team, they are more productive and enjoy improved mental health as well. According to recent research, many junior employees do not have enough opportunities to develop their decision-making skills since many bosses require them to follow only the supervisor's rules. If employees never have a chance to develop such skills and participate in teamwork, where will the company's future leaders come from? Therefore, if companies implement democratic leadership, I believe it will be a fascinating chance to develop employees' abilities.

prof.name: Professor Allen
prof.text: Psychologists have studied for decades what makes people happy. Which factor do you think contributes most to a person's overall happiness: their career, their personal relationships, or their health? Why?

students.name: Sofia
students.text: Personal relationships matter most. Studies show that people with close friends and family live longer and feel happier, no matter how much money they make.

students.name: James
students.text: Health is the foundation of everything. If you are sick, it is hard to enjoy your job or your relationships.

discussion.mine: I believe that career is the most factor that contribute to human happiness because it can be lead to a lot of opportunities in our daily lives. For example, people can get a lot of money and develop their dreams through developing their career. Furthermore, when people get a job, they can also get the quality of personal relationships because they usually spend a lot of time with their coworkers. It can lead to networking events. According to recent research, many older generations feel blue after retirement. Therefore, I believe developing one's career is the largest impact on their overall happiness.
discussion.tutor: I believe that career is the most important factor that contributes to human happiness because it can lead to a lot of opportunities in our daily lives. For example, people can earn a lot of money and realize their dreams through improving their career. Furthermore, when people get a job, they can also enhance the quality of personal relationships because they usually spend a lot of time with their coworkers. A good company job can also lead to networking events, another opportunity to meet interesting people. According to recent research, many older generations feel blue after retirement; therefore, I believe developing one's career has the largest impact on a person's overall happiness.

prof.name: Doctor Achebe
prof.text: As technology continues to evolve, educators are faced with the challenge of integrating new tools into their teaching practices. While some see these innovations as opportunities to enhance learning and engagement, others are concerned about potential classroom distractions caused by the use of technology and the impact on instructional quality. In what ways can technology be used thoughtfully to support, rather than detract from, the educational experience?

students.name: Paul
students.text: Integrating technology into education is essential for preparing students for a digital world. Tools like interactive apps, online resources, and virtual labs make learning more engaging and accessible to students who might otherwise have been disengaged with traditional teaching methods. When used thoughtfully, technology helps educators connect with students in ways that traditional methods would not.

students.name: Kelly
students.text: While technology can be helpful, it too often becomes a distraction in the classroom. Constant notifications and reliance on digital tools can reduce a student's ability to concentrate or think critically and independently. Sometimes, traditional teaching methods offer a structured learning experience that technology can unintentionally disrupt.

discussion.note: 10/25 감점 핵심: 질문은 'In what ways ... used thoughtfully' = 어떻게 써야 하나(방법). 내 글은 '기술이 좋다'(찬반)로 답함. 'In what ways / How' 질문엔 템플릿 첫 줄(Both A and B…) 대신 방법을 바로 말한다.
discussion.mine: Both Paul and Kelly made valid points, but I lean toward Paul's view. I strongly agree with the notion that integrating technology into education is crucial for students because technology can be used at anytime that students want. In the past, when students had a question, they had to wait until classes. However, technologies such as AI tools, and online resources, answers to students 24/7. Furthermore, it makes students save time and money. Instead of traditional private tutoring services, students can study effectively with technologies even they paid low prices. For these reasons, I believe using technologies is important for many students.
discussion.fix:
I believe technology should be used to support classroom learning rather than replace traditional teaching methods.

One major advantage is that students can use AI tools and online resources whenever they need help. In the past, students often had to wait until their next class to ask questions. However, AI tools can now answer students' questions 24/7. This also helps students save time and money because they can study effectively without paying for expensive private tutoring.

However, as Kelly mentioned, technology can also distract students. Therefore, teachers should encourage students to use digital tools for specific learning activities and limit unnecessary screen time during lessons.

For these reasons, I believe technology can improve education when it is used appropriately.

prof.name: Doctor Gupta
prof.text: In today's digital world, customer feedback and social media go hand in hand. Previously, businesses relied on surveys or comment cards to understand what customers thought. Now, with social media platforms, feedback is instant, public, and widespread, allowing for swift reactions from companies. However, this also means that negative opinions can impact a business faster and more deeply than ever before. With the rise of social media, how important is the role of customer feedback to businesses?

students.name: Andrew
students.text: I think companies place too much importance on people who like to complain a lot on social media. Happy customers are less likely to speak out on social media, so their voices are not heard. This leads businesses to make decisions based on the opinions of a few loud people instead of the majority of their customers.

students.name: Claire
students.text: Social media opens the door to a wider range of opinions, allowing more voices to be heard. This openness means companies can no longer ignore negative feedback by focusing on a few positive survey responses. As a result, companies have a more authentic view of customer satisfaction and areas for improvement, leading to more successful business strategies.

discussion.note: 질문(얼마나 중요한가)에는 맞게 답함 (10/25보다 나아짐). 이유 다음에 바로 결론으로 넘어가서 구체적 예시와 결과가 없음 → Opinion → Reason → Example → Result → Conclusion. feedback은 불가산 (feedbacks ✗). 'According to recent research'는 막연함.
discussion.mine: Both Andrew and Claire made valid points, but I believe that companies should accept various feedbacks from social media. This is because many people upload their feedback honestly on their social media. In the past, it was difficult to get specific reviews from traditional methods such as survey responses. However, nowadays, many people share their daily ideas on social media easily. According to recent research, if companies monitor these reviews on social media, it is helpful to utilize marketing strategies to improve their products. Therefore, I believe companies should accept users' feedbacks from social media.
discussion.fix:
I believe customer feedback on social media is extremely important for businesses because it helps them identify problems and improve their products.

Nowadays, many customers share their opinions and experiences on social media. Unlike traditional surveys, social media allows companies to receive feedback quickly and respond to customer concerns.

For example, if a clothing company receives complaints about the quality of its products, it can use this feedback to make improvements. This can increase customer satisfaction and build trust.

However, as Andrew mentioned, some online comments may not represent the opinions of most customers. Therefore, companies should consider a wide range of feedback before making decisions.

For these reasons, I believe social media feedback plays an essential role in helping businesses improve.

prof.name: Doctor Achebe
prof.text: Education and job training are rapidly evolving due to advancements in technology and changes in the job market. Therefore, the traditional four-year college model, where students spend years studying before entering the workforce, is being challenged. Alternatives like online courses, vocational training, and shorter degree programs promise quicker paths to employment. Taking these recent trends into account, is the traditional four-year college model still relevant in today's fast-paced, technology-driven world? Why or why not?

students.name: Claire
students.text: Personally, I believe shorter, more focused programs are better suited for people entering today's job market. These programs often focus on immediate, practical skills and allow learners to quickly pivot to new industries, like artificial intelligence or green energy, where traditional higher education courses may not be able to keep pace with the latest developments.

students.name: Andrew
students.text: I think traditional colleges are still relevant. They offer a broad range of subjects that allow students to explore different fields before deciding on a career path. This exploration is valuable and not something that can be easily replicated by online courses or short programs.

discussion.note: 약 96단어 (100 미만). 논리 비약: 주니어 일자리는 AI로 대체 → 회사는 시니어를 더 뽑음 → 그래서 대학. 쉽게 설명되는 이유 하나(폭넓은 지식 → 새 기술에 적응) + 예시(컴퓨터공학 학생)로 충분. 입장·이유·예시는 40초 안에 정하고, 표현이 5초 넘게 안 떠오르면 쉬운 말로 바꾼다. 10/28 튜터: 내 논리는 살리고 근거를 구체적으로 보강 — 'Some programmers are already being replaced by AI tools. However, research and development positions are still being actively hired for, and you cannot even apply to these positions without advanced degrees.'
discussion.mine: Both Claire and Andrew made valid points, but I lean toward Andrew's view. I agree with the notion that traditional four-year college model is still relevant because getting an advanced abilities is important in today's world. As Claire mentioned, practical skills allow learners to quickly pivot to new industries. However, it is limited to get a high-quality job. For example, many companies hire senior positions than junior positions since junior jobs can be replaced by technologies easily. For these reasons, io become a senior and advanced position members, I believe traditional college can help students effectively.
discussion.fix:
I believe the traditional four-year college model is still relevant because students need to develop advanced skills in today's rapidly changing world.

As Claire mentioned, short programs can help students learn practical skills quickly. However, these skills may become outdated as technology continues to develop. In contrast, traditional colleges provide students with broader knowledge and critical thinking skills.

For example, students who major in computer science can learn not only programming but also problem-solving skills. This knowledge can help them adapt to new technologies and take on more challenging tasks in their future careers.

Therefore, I believe traditional colleges still play an important role in preparing students for long-term career development.
discussion.tutor: Both Claire and Andrew made valid points, but I lean toward Andrew's view. I agree with the notion that the traditional four-year college model is still relevant because developing advanced abilities is still important in today's world. As Claire mentioned, practical skills allow learners to quickly pivot to new industries. However, these skills do not necessarily provide access to high-quality positions. For example, many companies hire senior positions more than junior positions, since the junior jobs can be replaced by technologies easily. Some programmers are already being replaced by AI tools. However, researcher and development positions are still being actively hired for, and you cannot even apply to these positions without advanced degrees. For these reasons, to obtain a senior or advanced position, I believe traditional college can help students achieve their goals more effectively.

prof.name: Doctor Achebe
prof.text: We've been discussing the role of social media in shaping public opinion. Social media platforms have become powerful tools not only for communication and information sharing, but also for influencing public opinion. Do you think social media has too much influence on public opinion? Why or why not?

students.name: Kelly
students.text: I believe social media has a positive influence on public opinion. It provides a powerful platform for people to raise awareness about important issues that affect peoples' everyday lives. It can also mobilize people for social causes and create a sense of community.

students.name: Paul
students.text: In my opinion, social media has a negative influence on public opinion. Because people often frequent sites that discuss issues that they are interested in, social media can lead to people only hearing opinions that reinforce their own beliefs. This can lead to a fragmented society.

discussion.note: 구조는 그대로 두고 표현만 교정 (the news media, manipulate people, faster, these). 결론의 'the most innovative platform'은 근거 없는 최상급 → an innovative, helpful platform.
discussion.mine: Both Kelly and Paul made valid points, but I lean toward Kelly's view. I agree with the notion that social media has a positive influence on public opinion because it provides an opportunity to express individuals' opinions more easily. For example, in the past, many governments tried to control news media in order to get a worth because many people get information only from news. However, this is impossible nowadays because people upload and express their opinions on social media easily. Furthermore, social media can deliver breaking news more fast. This is strongly advantageous when we are in emergency situations. For theses reasons, I believe social media is the most innovative platform in our daily lives.
discussion.tutor: Both Kelly and Paul made valid points, but I lean toward Kelly's view. I agree with the notion that social media has a positive influence on public opinion because it provides an opportunity to express individuals' opinions more easily. For example, in the past, many governments tried to control the news media in order to manipulate people because many people get their information only from the news. However, this is impossible nowadays because people upload and express their opinions on social media easily. Furthermore, social media can deliver breaking news faster. This is strongly advantageous when we are in emergency situations, for example. For these reasons, I believe social media is an innovative, helpful platform in our daily lives.

prof.name: Doctor Achebe
prof.text: Throughout history, artists have used their work to challenge societal norms and traditions as well as provoke thought. Some people believe that art should always aim to inspire and uplift, while others think it should confront and disrupt the status quo and stereotypes. What purpose do you think art should serve in society?

students.name: Claire
students.text: I believe art should inspire and uplift. In a world filled with challenges, art has the power to bring joy and hope to people who may need to escape from the pressures of everyday life. Art that is uplifting can improve a person's mental health.

students.name: Paul
students.text: I think art should confront and disrupt long held but outdated traditions and norms. Art has the ability to provoke thought and challenge people to see things from different perspectives. By addressing societal issues, art can drive change and promote progress.

discussion.note: 튜터가 결론에 반대 의견에 대한 반박을 추가: 'unlike Paul, I think people are challenged enough without the need to manufacture more provocations or challenges.' — 다른 학생 주장을 짚고 넘어가는 문장 1개.
discussion.mine: Both Claire and Paul made valid points, but I lean toward Claire's view. I agree with the notion that art should inspire and uplift because art can gives individual motivation in our daily lives. For example, I usually go to art museum and watch artistic objects on weekends. When I watched paintings from ancient, it made me reflect on my life. Honestly, I cannot exactly explain why it was inspired, but I had a dream to become a painting artist by these artistic masterpieces. Furthermore, when I commute to my university, I usually listen jazz music every morning. These music make me feel relaxed and comfortable. For these reasons, I believe art should inspire and uplift for many people.
discussion.tutor: Both Claire and Paul made valid points, but I lean toward Claire's view. I agree with the notion that art should inspire and uplift because art can give individual motivation in our daily lives. For example, I usually go to the art museum and look at artistic objects on weekends. When I see ancient paintings, it makes me reflect on my life. Honestly, I cannot exactly explain why I was so inspired, but I had a dream to become a painter because of these artistic masterpieces. Furthermore, when I commute to my university, I usually listen to jazz music every morning. This music makes me feel relaxed and comfortable. For these reasons, I believe art should inspire and uplift people; unlike Paul, I think people are challenged enough without the need to manufacture more provocations or challenges.

prof.name: Doctor Diaz
prof.text: We've been discussing the effects of different leadership styles on businesses. Some argue that authoritarian leadership, where a boss makes decisions with little input from their workers, is effective because it provides clear direction and expectations. Others believe that democratic leadership is better as it encourages employee participation and morale. Which leadership style do you think is more effective? Why?

students.name: Andrew
students.text: I think authoritarian leadership is more effective. It ensures that everyone knows their roles and responsibilities, which can increase productivity because workers are given clear directions for the job at hand. In high-pressure situations, clear direction can prevent confusion and mistakes.

students.name: Claire
students.text: I prefer democratic leadership. It values employees' input and can lead to more creative solutions and higher job satisfaction. When employees feel heard and valued, they are more motivated and committed to their work.

discussion.note: 튜터 x= on business → in business, junior jobs → entry-level. 뒷부분('Nowadays, many employees…' 이후)은 튜터가 대비 문장으로 다시 씀: In contrast to the traditional authoritarian leadership style, … increases their sense of 'ownership' … improve their communication skills. AD13(10/22)과 같은 주제.
discussion.mine: Both Andrew and Claire made valid points, but I lean toward Claire's view. I agree with the notion that democratic leadership is more effective on business because it can lead to productive results. For example, if leader encourages employee participation and morale on business, it will become a good opportunity to improve employee's abilities such as teamwork and making-decisions skills. Nowadays, many employees, especially many junior jobs, do not have enough opportunity to participate on business. I think it can limit productive results to companies. If companies access various opinions by democratic leadership, I believe it will be advantageous chances to results.
discussion.tutor: Both Andrew and Claire made valid points, but I lean toward Claire's view. I agree with the notion that democratic leadership is more effective on business because it can lead to productive results. For example, if a leader encourages employee participation and improved morale in business, it will become a good opportunity to improve employee's abilities in teamwork and decision-making skills. In contrast to the traditional authoritarian leadership style, democratic leadership that encourages participation allows employees to make important decisions in their companies, and this increases their sense of “ownership” in their workplace. Furthermore, they can improve their communication skills in the process.

ideas.note: 질문은 실전 기억, 학생 글은 '인프라·돈·경제 발전을 앞 학생이 다 말했다'는 기억으로 AI가 다시 씀. 당시 내 글: 국익 → 알리바바·타오바오 세금 → 정부 투자 (98단어에서 끝남).
ideas.q: Globalization has connected economies and societies around the world more closely than ever. Overall, do you think globalization has been good for society and the economy? Why or why not?

students.name: Kevin
students.text: I think globalization has been very positive. When foreign companies invest in a country, they build roads, ports, and factories. This infrastructure helps the whole economy grow, and countries that trade more become richer.

students.name: Sophia
students.text: I agree with Kevin. Global trade lets countries earn a lot of money by exporting their products. For example, many Asian countries developed their economies quickly because they could sell goods to the rest of the world.

angles.idea: 온라인 플랫폼으로 작은 가게도 전 세계에 판다 (기업·국가가 아닌 개인)

angles.idea: 맞벌이 부모는 두 달 돌봄 공백이 부담 → 짧은 방학이 가정에 더 현실적

angles.line: As a member of society, I would add that a year-round calendar is easier for working parents, who struggle to find childcare for two whole months.

angles.line: I agree with David, and as a consumer, I would add that customers suffer when services are unavailable one extra day.

angles.line: Squeezing five days of work into four creates long, exhausting days for employees.

angles.idea: 같은 비용으로 여러 콘텐츠를 누린다 (물건 하나 살 돈으로 다양한 자료)

angles.ex: A factory worker taking an online data course at night
angles.line: Short online programs give working adults and people in small towns a chance to learn new skills.

angles.idea: 정부가 뉴스를 통제하기 어려워졌다 → 영향력이 지나치지 않다 (오히려 필요)
angles.ex: Governments that once controlled the news media
angles.line: In the past, many governments tried to control the news media in order to manipulate people, but this is impossible nowadays because people express their opinions on social media.

angles.idea: 속보가 가장 빨리 전달된다
angles.ex: Real-time updates during a typhoon or earthquake
angles.line: Social media can deliver breaking news faster, which is strongly advantageous in emergency situations.

angles.idea: 확인 안 된 가짜 뉴스가 사실보다 빨리 퍼진다
angles.ex: False rumors about vaccines spreading during COVID-19
angles.line: Social media has too much influence because false information spreads faster than the truth.

angles.idea: 몇몇 회사의 알고리즘이 사람들이 볼 내용을 정한다
angles.ex: Trending topics chosen by an algorithm, not by people
angles.line: A few tech companies' algorithms decide what millions of people see, which gives them too much power.

angles.idea: Claire 확장 + Paul 반박: 사람들은 이미 충분히 힘들다, 굳이 도발을 더 만들 필요 없다
angles.ex: Ordinary people already facing stress at work and school
angles.line: Unlike Paul, I think people are challenged enough without the need to manufacture more provocations or challenges.

angles.idea: Claire 확장: 주말 미술관·출근길 재즈가 내 삶을 돌아보게 하고 꿈을 줬다
angles.ex: Ancient paintings at the art museum and jazz on the morning commute
angles.line: When I see ancient paintings, it makes me reflect on my life.

angles.idea: 제3의 목적: 예술은 역사를 기록해 다음 세대가 기억하게 한다
angles.ex: Picasso's Guernica recording the bombing of a town
angles.line: I feel that art should record history so that future generations never forget important events.

angles.idea: 제3의 목적: 공공 예술이 동네 사람들을 모은다
angles.ex: Residents painting murals together in Seoul's Ihwa Mural Village
angles.line: I believe art should bring communities together, as public mural projects do.

ideas.q: Cities have limited budgets for transportation. Should a city spend more money on improving public transportation, such as buses and subways, or on building and repairing roads for cars? Why?

students.name: Daniel
students.text: Public transportation is the better choice. If more people take buses and subways, there will be fewer cars on the road, so traffic jams will decrease. This saves everyone time.

students.name: Mia
students.text: I also prefer public transportation because it is better for the environment. Cars produce a lot of air pollution, and buses and trains can carry many people while producing much less carbon dioxide.

angles.idea: 차가 없는 사람에게 대중교통은 일자리·학교로 가는 유일한 수단
angles.ex: Students and part-time workers without cars commuting by subway
angles.line: Public transportation gives people who cannot afford a car equal access to jobs and education.

angles.idea: 운전 못 하는 사람의 이동권
angles.ex: Elderly people who stopped driving using low-floor buses
angles.line: Better public transportation lets elderly and disabled people move around the city independently.

angles.idea: 트럭·구급차·소방차는 도로가 있어야 움직인다
angles.ex: Delivery trucks and ambulances stuck on broken roads
angles.line: Roads are still essential because delivery trucks and ambulances cannot use subways.

angles.idea: 버스가 드문 지역은 결국 차가 필요하다
angles.ex: Rural towns where a bus comes only twice a day
angles.line: In suburbs and rural areas, good roads help more people than buses that rarely come.

ideas.q: Social media has become a major part of teenagers' lives. Do you think social media has a more positive or more negative effect on teenagers? Why?

students.name: Emma
students.text: I think it is mostly positive. Teenagers can stay connected with their friends anytime, even when they move to a different city or school. This helps them feel less lonely.

students.name: Jason
students.text: I disagree. Social media is harmful to teenagers' mental health. They constantly compare themselves to others' perfect photos, which makes them feel anxious and unhappy with their own lives.

angles.idea: 무료 강의·진로 정보를 SNS로 얻는다
angles.ex: Learning coding or drawing from YouTube and Instagram tutorials
angles.line: Social media helps teenagers discover new skills and career paths for free.

angles.idea: 주변에 없는 같은 관심사 친구를 찾는다
angles.ex: A teenager in a small town joining an online club for rare hobbies
angles.line: Social media lets teenagers find communities that do not exist in their own neighborhood.

angles.idea: 밤늦게까지 스크롤해서 잠·성적이 떨어진다
angles.ex: Scrolling short videos until 2 a.m. before an exam
angles.line: Social media takes away teenagers' sleep and focus, which hurts their grades.

angles.idea: 사진·위치 공개로 범죄·사이버 폭력 위험
angles.ex: Location tags revealing a student's school and home
angles.line: Teenagers often share too much personal information online, which can put their safety at risk.

ideas.q: Some universities require all students to study a foreign language, regardless of their major. Do you think universities should have this requirement? Why or why not?

students.name: Olivia
students.text: Yes, they should. Speaking a second language is a big advantage in the job market. Many companies work with international partners, so they prefer to hire employees who can speak another language.

students.name: Ryan
students.text: I don't think so. Students have limited time, and they should focus on courses related to their major. An engineering student, for instance, needs more math and science, not a language class.

angles.idea: 다른 언어를 배우면 다른 관점으로 생각하는 법을 배운다
angles.ex: Learning that some languages have no future tense
angles.line: Learning a foreign language teaches students to see the world from a different point of view.

angles.idea: 교환학생·여행에서 현지인과 진짜 관계를 맺는다
angles.ex: An exchange student in Spain making local friends
angles.line: A foreign language lets students build real relationships during exchange programs and travel.

angles.idea: 번역 앱·AI 때문에 필요성이 줄었다
angles.ex: Using Papago or AI translation during a business trip
angles.line: With modern translation tools, a required language class is less useful than before.

angles.idea: 억지로 듣는 수업은 효과 없고 등록금만 든다
angles.ex: Students forgetting a required language two years later
angles.line: Students learn best when they choose a language because they want to, not because it is required.

ideas.q: Many companies now allow employees to work from home several days a week. Do you think working from home is better or worse for companies overall? Why?

students.name: Lucas
students.text: It is better. Employees save a lot of time because they don't have to commute, so they have more energy for their work and become more productive.

students.name: Hannah
students.text: I think it is worse. When people are not in the same office, communication becomes difficult. Small questions take longer to answer, and teamwork suffers.

angles.idea: 지역 제한 없이 전국·해외 인재를 뽑는다
angles.ex: A Seoul startup hiring a developer living in Busan
angles.line: Remote work lets companies hire talented people from anywhere, not just near the office.

angles.idea: 사무실 임대료·관리비가 줄어든다
angles.ex: A company moving to a smaller office and saving rent
angles.line: Companies can save a large amount of money on office rent when employees work from home.

angles.idea: 신입은 옆에서 보고 배우는 기회를 잃는다
angles.ex: A new employee who never sees how seniors handle clients
angles.line: New employees learn much more slowly when they cannot watch experienced coworkers in person.

angles.idea: 집 와이파이·개인 노트북으로 정보 유출 위험
angles.ex: Confidential files on a shared family computer
angles.line: Working from home increases the risk that important company information will leak.

ideas.q: Some cities have banned private cars from their downtown areas. Do you think this is a good policy? Why or why not?

students.name: Noah
students.text: I support this policy because cars cause serious air pollution. Without cars downtown, the air would be much cleaner and healthier for everyone.

students.name: Grace
students.text: I agree. Downtown areas always have terrible traffic. If cars are banned, buses can move faster and people can get where they need to go more easily.

angles.idea: 걷는 사람이 늘면 가게 매출이 오른다
angles.ex: Car-free streets in Copenhagen with busy outdoor cafés
angles.line: When people walk instead of drive, they stop at more shops, which helps local businesses.

angles.idea: 보행자 교통사고가 줄어든다
angles.ex: Fewer accidents involving children near downtown schools
angles.line: Banning cars makes downtown streets much safer for pedestrians, especially children.

angles.idea: 물건 납품·배달이 어려워진다
angles.ex: Store owners unable to receive deliveries during the day
angles.line: A car ban makes it hard for downtown stores to receive goods and deliver to customers.

angles.idea: 걷기 힘든 사람은 도심 접근이 막힌다
angles.ex: An elderly patient who must drive to a downtown hospital
angles.line: People who cannot walk long distances could lose access to downtown hospitals and offices.

ideas.q: AI tools like chatbots can now write essays and solve math problems. Should schools allow students to use AI tools for their homework? Why or why not?

students.name: Chloe
students.text: Yes. AI tools can explain difficult concepts quickly, so students can learn more efficiently and finish their homework faster.

students.name: Ethan
students.text: No. Students will just copy answers from AI without thinking. This is cheating, and they will not actually learn anything.

angles.idea: 회사에서 AI를 쓰니 학교에서 제대로 쓰는 법을 배워야 한다
angles.ex: Office workers using AI to draft reports
angles.line: Schools should teach students how to use AI well, because they will need this skill at work.

angles.idea: 과외 받을 돈 없는 학생에게 무료 개인 교사
angles.ex: A student who cannot afford a tutor asking AI at midnight
angles.line: AI tools give students who cannot afford private tutors a free source of help.

angles.idea: AI가 틀린 정보를 그럴듯하게 말한다
angles.ex: A chatbot inventing a fake historical date
angles.line: AI tools often give wrong information confidently, and students may not notice the mistakes.

angles.idea: 숙제로는 학생 실력을 알 수 없어 교사가 도울 수 없다
angles.ex: A teacher who thinks a student understands because the homework is perfect
angles.line: If students use AI, teachers cannot see what their students actually need help with.

ideas.q: Some young people go to university right after high school, while others start working first. Which do you think is better for young people? Why?

students.name: Ava
students.text: Going to university is better. People with a university degree usually earn higher salaries and have more job opportunities over their lifetime.

students.name: Liam
students.text: I think working first is better. University is very expensive, and many students end up with large debts. Working first lets young people save money.

angles.idea: 일해 보면 무엇을 전공할지 분명해진다 (일 먼저)
angles.ex: Working at a café and discovering an interest in business
angles.line: Working first helps young people find out what they really want to study.

angles.idea: 대학에서 평생 갈 인맥·친구를 만든다 (대학 먼저)
angles.ex: Classmates who later start a company together
angles.line: University gives young people a network of friends and contacts that lasts for life.

angles.idea: 일 먼저 하면 공부 습관이 끊겨 돌아가기 어렵다
angles.ex: Friends who planned to go back to school but never did
angles.line: Once young people start earning money, it becomes very hard to return to studying.

angles.idea: 일하면서 책임감·시간 관리를 배운다
angles.ex: Learning to manage a schedule at a part-time job
angles.line: Working first teaches young people responsibility that makes them better students later.

ideas.q: Space exploration programs cost governments billions of dollars. Do you think governments should continue to spend money on space exploration? Why or why not?

students.name: Isabella
students.text: Yes. Space programs create new technologies that we use every day, such as GPS and better medical equipment. This research benefits everyone.

students.name: Mason
students.text: No. There are many problems on Earth, like poverty and hunger. The money should be used to help people who are struggling right now.

angles.idea: 우주 탐사가 학생들을 과학·공학으로 끌어들인다
angles.ex: Students choosing engineering after watching a Mars landing
angles.line: Space exploration inspires young people to study science and engineering.

angles.idea: 위성으로 기후·산불·홍수를 감시한다
angles.ex: Satellites tracking wildfires and typhoons
angles.line: Space programs help us protect the Earth by watching climate change and natural disasters from above.

angles.idea: SpaceX처럼 민간이 더 싸게 하니 세금은 다른 곳에
angles.ex: SpaceX reusable rockets cutting launch costs
angles.line: Private companies can now explore space more cheaply, so governments should spend tax money elsewhere.

angles.idea: 위성 경쟁이 우주 쓰레기·충돌 위험을 키운다
angles.ex: Thousands of broken satellites orbiting the Earth
angles.line: More space programs create dangerous space debris that could damage important satellites.

ideas.q: Tourism has grown rapidly in many small towns and villages. Overall, do you think tourism is good or bad for local communities? Why?

students.name: Sarah
students.text: Tourism is good because it brings money and jobs. Hotels, restaurants, and shops all need workers, so local people have more ways to earn a living.

students.name: David
students.text: I think it is bad. Too many tourists create pollution and crowds. The streets become dirty and noisy, and nature gets damaged.

angles.idea: 관광객 관심 덕분에 사라질 전통이 보존된다
angles.ex: Traditional hanok villages restored because of visitors
angles.line: Tourism can help small towns protect traditions that might otherwise disappear.

angles.idea: 에어비앤비 때문에 집값·월세가 올라 주민이 떠난다
angles.ex: Residents in Barcelona or Jeju pushed out by rising rent
angles.line: Tourism raises housing prices so much that local residents can no longer afford to live there.

angles.idea: 관광객 취향에 맞춘 똑같은 가게만 남는다
angles.ex: Every street filled with the same souvenir shops and chain cafés
angles.line: Tourism can turn unique towns into places that all look the same.

angles.idea: 외부 사람과 교류하며 주민이 자기 지역에 자부심을 갖는다
angles.ex: Elderly villagers teaching visitors how to make kimchi
angles.line: Meeting visitors from other places makes local people proud of their community.

email: 요구사항 3개를 모두, 각각 설명 한 문장씩 더해서

100–130단어 · 2–3문단 · 'I hope this email finds you well.'은 따로 한 줄

ideaSwitch: 튜터: 교수 질문에 집중하고 학생 글은 훑기만. 계획 1–2분 = 나만의 'original content'
튜터: 다른 학생은 무시해도 되지만, 실수로 그들의 주장을 반복하지 말 것
전략 1 (튜터): 완전히 다른 것 말하기 — Although A and B both have good ideas, I feel …
전략 2 (튜터): 한 학생 주장 넓히기 — I agree with B, and I would further her argument … 단 B와 꽤 다른 내 내용이 있어야 높은 점수대 (MUST)
튜터 템플릿 주어: As a [student / consumer / member of society], I would add that … — 앞 학생이 국가·기업 얘기를 했으면 이 주어로 내려간다
튜터가 칭찬한 예 (9/16 구독): 앞 학생이 '초기 비용 낮음'·'장기적으로 비쌈'을 말했을 때 '같은 비용으로 다양한 콘텐츠' 관점 — Good!
AI 정리 (10/31 실전): 같은 예시도 주어를 바꾸면 새 아이디어 (타오바오: 정부 세금 → 작은 판매자). 인과 사슬을 3단계 넘게 늘이지 않는다
discussion: 교수 질문을 먼저 읽고 학생 글은 훑기 (1분) · 계획 1–2분 · 쓰기 6–7분 · 검토 1분
질문이 How / In what ways면 찬반이 아니라 '방법'을 답한다. 첫 문장 = 방법 한 줄 (10/25 감점)
40초 안에 입장 + 이유 1개 + 예시 1개를 정하고, 쓰는 도중엔 바꾸지 않는다. 표현이 5초 넘게 안 떠오르면 쉬운 말로 (10/27)
Opinion → Reason → Example → Result → Conclusion: 이유 다음에 바로 결론으로 넘어가지 말 것 (10/27)
120–140단어, 내 주제 문장이 질문의 핵심 명사와 맞는지
이름·장소·숫자가 있는 구체적 예시 1개 ('recent research'는 막연함)
'그래서 어떻게 되는가' 문장 1개 더 (튜터가 매번 추가한 부분)
다른 학생 주장을 반복하지 말고 넓히거나 다른 것을 말하기
